observations: body L1-L39: the Addenda to the second volume, continued; the page numbers stand bold at the head of the entries, and the numbers corrected and their corrections are italic.
body L1-L4: «de Goeje» and «Marquart» are letter-spaced; «Mémoire sur les migrations des Tsiganes» «à travers l'Asie» and «An-Nīrūn» are italic. The e of «appellant» (L4) prints broken.

body L5: the words of the titles in Arabic letters: «جزءً» has the tanwīn of the accusative over the hamza and no alif after it, «جزءًا» the alif. Two specks above the ‘ayn of «وعرف» are not transcribed.

body L7-L8: the numbers in Arabic letters, «نب» 52 and «يب» 12, «مد نز» 44 57 and «مه يز» 45 17, agree with the Latin numbers beside them. The restored numbers are italic, while «12″» (L8) is roman. A blot (3.7 by 3.2 pt) to the right of L8 is not transcribed.

body L10-L11: the numbers in Arabic letters follow the western (Maghribi) values of the letters, in which ض is 90 and س 300: «قضا يو» 191 16, «سمح مد» 348 44, «قض نو» 190 56 and «سمط د» 349 4, as the Latin numbers beside them; the same correction is given for p. 32 on p. XXVIII (L1). The final ḥā’ of «سمح» has the hooked head of the final jīm of «الخليــج» on p. XXIV. «349° 4′» is roman.
body L12: the dash measures 10.0 pt.

body L13-L17: «يو لب» 16 32 and «يو لط» 16 39, «كد» 24 and «كد ه» 24 5, «مح يج» 48 13 and «مح نج» 48 53, «يد» 14 and «يه» 15 agree with the Latin numbers beside them. In «مح» the mīm stands above the ḥā’; the hā’ of «كد ه» has its looped form.
body L15: the h of «2h» is a small raised italic h.
body L19: «142–143» (bold) and «1–3» have long dashes (5.2 and 4.9 pt).
body L20-L21: the d of «consulenda» prints broken; the 6 of «16» (L21) prints without its stem, so that it looks like a 0.

body L23-L26: «Ibn al-Athīr» and «Abū ’l-fidā’» are letter-spaced; «Baṭlīmūs ibn Lāghūs», «Annales», «Historia anteislamica», «Baṭlamyūs Sūtīr», «ibn Lāghūs» and «al-Man-» «ṭiqī» are italic, and the t of «Sūtīr» has no dot. «σωτήρ» has the acute, its η printed with the short upright stroke after it; «سشون» is the reading of the editions. The sign = of L24 is printed long (9.5 pt).

body L27-L35: the entry on pp. 194-195, «194–195» bold, with a long dash. The Syriac words are printed in a West Syriac (Serto) type with the Greek vowel signs of that script and set here in an Estrangela type: «ܡܰܡܰܐ» (L27, L30) with the ptāḥā (a) over each mīm, and «ܡܰܡܰܐܝܰܐ» (L30) with the ptāḥā over the two mīms and the yōdh. «Payne-Smith», «Assemani», «Bar ‘Alī», «Lidzbarski», «Abū ’l-faraǵ», «Barhebraeus» and «Hartmann» are letter-spaced; «Māmā», «Thesauro», «Ephemeris für semitische» «Epigraphik», «longas», «Māmāy» and «Māmāyah» are italic. The dash of L31 measures 9.7 pt; a mark under the u of «genuina» (L33) is a speck.
body L36-L39: «Basset» and «al–‘Ayyāshī» are letter-spaced; «Daqyūs» (L36) and «Riḥlah» are italic, «Daqyūs» in L39 roman. «boreo–occidentalis» and «al–‘Ayyāshī» have long dashes (5.3 and 5.5 pt).

notes_left L1-L6, notes_right L1-L6: three notes in two columns with a thin rule between them; note 2 runs from the left column into the right, and note 3 continues on p. XXX. «Basset» and «Mouliéras» are letter-spaced; «Chronicon Syriacum», «No-» «tes de lexicographie berbère: le dialecte des Beni» «Menacer», «Le Maroc inconnu» and «Taqiyūs» are italic.
notes_left L1: the stop after «l» prints as a tiny dot (0.4 pt).

notes_left L3: the passage of Barhebraeus' Chronicon, printed in the West Syriac type and set in Estrangela: «ܐܠܟܣܢܕܪܘܣ ܩܣܪ ܒܪ ܡܐܡܐ», Alexander Caesar, son of Māmā, the long vowels of the name written with ālaph.
source_authority: Controlling master page image. Embedded text is not the authority for a reading.
transcription_convention: Source line breaks, hyphenation, quotation signs and word-level type distinctions retained. L numbers count text-bearing lines.
review_responsibility: Transcribed by Claude from the page images; Greek, Arabic, numbers and signs read on enlarged images. Not reviewed by a person.
